entities.summary: Nathaniel William Taylor was an influential Protestant Theologian of the early 19th century, whose major contribution to the Christian faith, known as the New Haven theology or Taylorism, was to line up historical Calvinism with the religious revivalism of the time. A graduate of Yale College, he returned to found the school's first independent division, the Theological Department, an institution which later became the Yale Divinity School.
